result:
Every neighborhood has a place that appears to do nothing.

Mine has a narrow bench beside a brick wall. It faces neither the park nor the street, only a patch of gravel where weeds keep trying their luck. Someone painted it green years ago, and someone else carved a name into one armrest. The name has weathered until it could belong to almost anyone.

I used to pass it without looking. Then one afternoon, caught between errands and unwilling to go home, I sat down.

From there I noticed the small traffic of the place: ants following a crack in the pavement, a moth tucked into the mortar, a grocery receipt turning slowly in the breeze. A man walked past carrying a cake box with both hands. He looked at me, then at the bench, as if wondering whether there was a reason to sit there.

There wasn’t, exactly. But I moved over anyway.
